patches.name: bash53-001
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-001 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it: In posix mode, `wait -n' with pid arguments does not restrict the set of processes it considers to those arguments.

patches.name: bash53-002
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-002 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it: There are too many differences in the various implementations of shm_open(2) to rely on it for bash's use.

patches.name: bash53-003
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-003 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it: Bash leaves internal quoting in place when expanding array subscripts that appear inside array subscripts in an arithmetic context, causing expansion failures.

patches.name: bash53-004
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-004 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it: The Linux kernel reports incorrect sizes for files in /sys/block/*/uevent, leading bash to report a read error when the byte count does not agree with the file size from fstat(2).

patches.name: bash53-005
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-005 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it: Restoring the default disposition in a subshell for a signal bash treats specially can cause a crash.

patches.name: bash53-006
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-006 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it: When `globasciiranges' is enabled, glob patterns with ranges in bracket expressions can produce incorrect matches for character ranges whose start and end are non-ascii characters.

patches.name: bash53-007
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-007 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it: No-fork command substitutions can perform redirections that act on the enclosing command as well.

patches.name: bash53-008
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-008 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it: Bash tries to consume entire multibyte characters when looking for backslash escapes in $'...' strings, and treats too many characters as potentially beginning a multibyte character in UTF-8 locales. Being more selective about when to call mbrtowc() can lead to optimized string processing and script speedups. This patch also handles the unlikely situation of a locale encoding null wide characters with non-null bytes.

patches.name: bash53-009
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-009 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it: A SIGINT during a reverse i-search can cause a segmentation fault due to accessing data freed by a signal handler.

patches.name: bash53-010
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-010 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it:

patches.name: bash53-011
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-011 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it: If a `mapfile' callback unsets the array variable `mapfile' is using to save the lines it reads, `mapfile' can try to reference freed memory, which can cause corruption or shell crashes.

patches.name: bash53-012
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-012 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it: If a subshell with an inherited EXIT trap receives a fatal signal before it clears the exit trap, and before it restores its original signal handlers, it's possible for it to inappropriately run the inherited EXIT trap.

patches.name: bash53-013
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-013 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it: Comparing the value of a pointer returned from realloc/xrealloc to the original pointer passed is technically undefined behavior, which matters under some circumstances.

patches.name: bash53-014
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-014 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it: Bash-5.3 patch 11 included an inadvertent extra line, which this patch removes. This also takes the opportunity to improve that patch, by looking up the variable each time through the line-reading loop only if there is a callback and it is invoked.

patches.name: bash53-015
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-015 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it: There are circumstances under which index -1 is used to reference into the input buffer used by the `read' builtin.

patches.name: bash53-016
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-016 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it: On recent versions of macOS, the pipe size is dynamic and changes due to system-wide total pipe usage, so we have to check whether or not bash can use the size determined at compile time.

patches.name: bash53-017
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-017 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it: If readline is invoked with the cursor somewhere other than column 0, and the prompt contains multibyte characters, the display algorithm needs to use a buffer offset, instead of the physical prompt length, to determine whether or not to reprint the prompt from column 0 because the cursor is before the last invisible character in the prompt string.

patches.name: bash53-018
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-018 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it:

patches.name: bash53-019
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-019 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it: On some systems, macOS in particular, isalpha(3) returns true for bytes between 128 and 255. Bash uses this to determine whether or not these characters are permitted to be part of a shell identifier, and can consume one byte too many when determining the end of a variable name.

patches.name: bash53-020
patches.purpose: The official patch bash53-020 to GNU Bash 5.3, byte for byte as ftp.gnu.org publishes it: If readline handles a SIGWINCH and resizes its idea of the screen dimensions, it needs to recompute the columns where the prompt wraps lines every time, not just when the screen width decreases.

patches.name: readline-reader-mailbox
patches.purpose: A private mailbox the bundled Readline reads once it has consumed everything it had buffered and is waiting for the terminal, and which it waits on alongside the terminal; the counts the reader holds privately, for the fence proof; the input source of each character; a non-destructive cancellation through Readline's own abort path; the reader's own enter and leave boundaries; and the end-of-file decision immediately before Readline's own end-of-file branch, which leaves the shell's ignoreeof setting alone.

patches.name: readline-reader-state
patches.purpose: The reader states the detach condition and the cancellation report are evaluated against, where Readline keeps no flag of its own: a quoted insertion waiting for its character, and an open bracketed paste.

patches.name: bash-bridge-activation
patches.purpose: The bridge loads before the user's startup files and before the first primary reader, and the `kr-bridge` builtin the guarded startup entry activates the user-facing hooks through.

patches.name: bash-command-resolve
patches.purpose: The executor asks the integration before it forks a command of the accepted line that the root shell starts itself, in the foreground and with no pipe, and the forked child starts the launcher the answer names in its place, with the backend's variables added; any other answer, and a launcher that cannot be started, leave the command exactly as it was typed.

startup.target: $HOME/.bashrc, or the first login file read when that file does not source it
